items.confound_note: All four segments sit inside the same month, so one site-wide discount covers every case at once, and every segment browsed the general catalogue where that discount applied. Each segment is compared against itself a month earlier, before the discount ran, so the discount and the new page changed together and the evidence cannot separate them. The coherent_true item states the same discount but puts every segment on a fixed-price contract catalogue, which is what makes it sound.
items.notes: SEED. Cases identical to coherent_true; only the closer differs. The discount works as a single confound precisely because all four segments share the same month.

Two: mobile sessions from Portugal via email switched on 3 June; by 27 June cart additions ran 4 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Three: tablet sessions from Kenya via referral switched on 5 September; by 30 September cart additions ran 7 percent above the same segment a month earlier.

items.passage:
An analytics log records four session segments after the checkout page was replaced.
One: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 4 March; by 29 March cart additions ran 6 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Two: mobile sessions from Portugal via email switched on 3 June; by 27 June cart additions ran 4 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Three: tablet sessions from Kenya via referral switched on 5 September; by 30 September cart additions ran 7 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Four: kiosk sessions from Japan via display switched on 2 November; by 26 November cart additions ran 5 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Prices held steady through each segment's month, matching the earlier period to the nearest cent, and every segment browsed a fixed-price contract catalogue; traffic volume and product range were unchanged, and no other release shipped.
items.confound_note: Every case measures cart additions, not purchases. Putting an item in a cart is not buying it, and a checkout page can raise cart additions while completed purchases stay flat or fall - abandonment at checkout is exactly what this page governs. The claim is about purchases, so none of the four cases speaks to it.
items.notes: SEED. Closer identical to both TRUE items. The flaw is that the measured quantity is not the claimed one. A shared confound is unavailable here because the four segments span four months, four countries, four devices and four sources.
